description: We’re a team of curious builders who love space, tech, and solving interesting problems.
summary:
Red-Rock is an interactive Mars surface exploration and decision-support platform designed to help astronauts understand unfamiliar terrain, accomplish scientific objectives, and navigate more safely. It combines NASA Mars datasets, including topographic, thermal, optical, and mission-derived data, into a unified, location-aware interface.

Instead of simply displaying a map of Mars, Red-Rock transforms scientific observations into actionable context. Astronauts can explore a location, examine its terrain and environmental characteristics, identify potential hazards and scientifically relevant areas, and plan routes that prioritize safety rather than simply minimizing distance. The platform can also provide mission imagery and data-confidence context to help crews understand what they may encounter.

This addresses the challenge by combining multiple NASA data types into a practical surface exploration tool centered on astronaut safety and scientific objectives. Red-Rock is important because Mars exploration requires decisions in environments where conditions are unfamiliar and data can be incomplete or uncertain. Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex planetary science and understandable operational decisions: explore Mars, understand the risks, and find the safer way.
details:
Red-Rock is an interactive Mars surface exploration and decision-support platform designed to help astronauts understand unfamiliar environments, plan scientific activities, and navigate more safely. The system combines multiple NASA Mars datasets into a unified 3D interface rather than treating each dataset as a separate map layer.

An astronaut can explore a location on Mars, examine terrain and environmental information, identify potential hazards and scientifically relevant areas, and plan a route to a target. Red-Rock’s routing concept prioritizes safety factors rather than simply selecting the shortest path. The platform also provides contextual information about the underlying data so that users can understand the basis and uncertainty of an assessment.

The project’s main benefit is turning complex planetary-science data into information that can support human exploration decisions. Its intended impact is to make Mars surface exploration more informed, safer, and easier to understand while helping astronauts reach scientific targets efficiently.

We developed the project using React and TypeScript for the frontend, Tailwind CSS for the interface, and Three.js for the interactive 3D Mars visualization. The backend uses Node.js, TypeScript, Express.js, and npm. GDAL and Rasterio are used for processing scientific raster datasets and Turf.js for geospatial calculations. We also use graph-based/A* routing concepts for safety-aware navigation, with Neon and Vercel supporting deployment.

Codex agents played an important role in development. We used multiple specialized coding agents to work on different parts of the system, including backend architecture, NASA data integration, geospatial processing, Mars intelligence, routing, and API development. The agents were coordinated around a shared architecture so that their work could be integrated into one functioning application rather than producing isolated prototypes.

The project is creative because it goes beyond visualizing Mars. It creates an intelligence layer between scientific data and astronaut decisions: NASA data → context → risk understanding → route planning → action.

Our team considered astronaut safety, scientific usefulness, data provenance, uncertainty, terrain difficulty, route length, computational practicality, data availability, and the limitations of current Mars observations. We also considered how the interface could eventually function as a tablet, mission-console, or other astronaut-facing exploration tool.

Red-Rock is ultimately designed around one principle: Mars should not be treated as just a map. It is an environment with constraints, uncertainty, and scientific opportunities, and our system helps turn those complexities into understandable exploration decisions.
